# testdata/ — the regression library

A synthetic twin of every byte shape in the owner's corpus (`exemplars.yaml`, 86 entries over 33 mimes) for
spec + tooling regression testing, plus the regression ontology those bytes classify under. Every
fixture is generated by a script kept beside it (see "The synthetic tier" and `synthetic/gen/COVERAGE.md`);
no private byte is in the set and nothing waits on a placement.

Tracked here: this README, `exemplars.yaml` (the manifest — file, blake3, mime, root term, shape
and a neutral technical note, no personal content), `seed.ts` (the seeder), `ontology/` (the
regression ontology a standalone instance starts from), `passes/` (the generated pass of the asserted-tree PDF) and `synthetic/`.
**`instance/` is never tracked** — the scratch layer `seed.ts` builds is gitignored at the repo root
(`/testdata/instance/`), as is `/testdata/regression/`, where private bytes once sat; nothing reads it.

### The synthetic tier

Fixtures with no private content, committed under `testdata/synthetic/` with manifest entries pointing at
them, and the script that generates each one kept under `testdata/synthetic/gen/`
(see `gen/README.md` for the tool and version behind every file). The committed bytes, not a fresh run of
a generator, are what the manifest's blake3 pins: an encoder's output drifts across tool versions even for
identical input, so
pinning a freshly-generated hash would make the manifest non-reproducible from one machine or ffmpeg/libheif
version to the next. The text formats the scripts write themselves do reproduce byte-for-byte.

### Generated twins (`synthetic/gen/`)

Every regression artifact is a *twin*: a fixture with the same shape as a private artifact of the owner's corpus
and fictional content, generated by a script kept under `synthetic/gen/` (`COVERAGE.md` there is the inventory
of shapes). `gen/plain.ts`
makes the twins whose test is classify + attest + lint (the readme, the script, the address book and cards,
the exchange file, the media manifest, the screenshot, the photograph with its Exif orientation, the clip,
the receipt). `gen/thread.ts`, `gen/mailing.ts`, `gen/novel.ts`, `gen/chat-archive.ts` and `gen/chat-export.ts`
make the full-shape twins of the thread capture, the mailing, the novel, the mailbox slice and the chat export,
each with a regression leg of its own and frozen counts. `gen/procedure.ts` makes the asserted-tree PDF, a fictional calculation procedure in the shape of a methodological tool: one content model drives both the typst source
(`procedure.typ`, rendered to `procedure.pdf` with typst 0.15.1 and its bundled fonts; `set document(date:
none)` makes the render byte-identical across runs) and the pass lines (`passes/<blake3>.p1.jsonl`), whose
boxes are read back off the rendered PDF through `pdf.words@1`. Re-rendering is re-running the script; the
committed PDF is what the manifest pins, and a changed render is a new blake3, a new pass file and a new pin
in the test, on purpose.

### The regression ontology

`ontology/` is the ontology every test instance copies in (`ath/test/layers.ts`): the
methodological-tool terms, the XenForo and Amazon expression roots, and a root term per mime. Edit it here; `ath ontology lint` over a fresh standalone instance is the gate.

## Seeding a scratch instance

```
bun testdata/seed.ts                              # the synthetic/ bytes
bun testdata/seed.ts --from /path/to/source/instance   # also pull missing bytes by blake3
```

Idempotent — an entry whose subject already exists in `instance/` is skipped, so re-running after
adding a manifest entry only seeds what's new. A container's members (zip, epub, mbox, a message's
attachments) become subjects of their own.

Sanity-check after seeding:

```
bun ath/src/main.ts --root testdata/instance lint --all
```
